author: Walt7
title: Mouse Without Borders: manually entered security key/PC name fields get wiped instantly on "Connect" click — must not clear user input

status.label: Fix plan ready for design
status.detail: The current Settings page unconditionally clears both input boxes after the async connection request returns, including failure paths.

next_action.label: Design fix
next_action.reason: Preserve user-entered values unless the connection request succeeds, and add focused failure-path coverage before implementation.

judgment.rationale: The report gives a deterministic reproduction and the current upstream code directly confirms the data-loss mechanism: Connect() awaits SubmitConnectionRequestAsync and then clears both text boxes without checking success or exception outcome.
evidence: The reporter reproduces the issue by entering a security key and device name, clicking Connect, and observing both fields cleared with no visible connection or error.
MouseWithoutBordersPage.xaml.cs reads both fields, awaits SubmitConnectionRequestAsync, then unconditionally assigns String.Empty to ConnectPCNameTextBox.Text and ConnectSecurityKeyTextBox.Text.
The issue includes a successful Test-NetConnection to port 15101 and a current PowerToys 0.101.2362 WinGet installation, narrowing the report away from a simple reachability failure.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a focused design to preserve input on failed connection attempts and test both success and failure paths.

fix_assessment.rationale: No linked fix attempt is present. The defect is in PowerToys Settings UI behavior and is directly actionable in the current connection command path.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve Mouse Without Borders connection inputs on failure
proposed_fixes.root_cause: MouseWithoutBordersPage.Connect clears both TextBox values after awaiting SubmitConnectionRequestAsync regardless of whether the request connected, failed, or reported an error.
plan: Inspect the result and error contract of MouseWithoutBordersViewModel.SubmitConnectionRequestAsync.
Clear the security-key and device-name TextBox values only after a confirmed successful connection; preserve them and surface the existing error path otherwise.
Add focused Settings UI coverage for successful submission, failed submission, and exception/error return so manually entered values remain available for retry.
verification: Run the focused Mouse Without Borders Settings UI tests.
Enter a key and device name, force a failed connection, and verify both values remain visible.
Repeat with a successful connection and verify the fields clear only after success.

confidence.rationale: The unconditional clear is visible in the exact current source method and matches the reported symptom; only the success-result API shape needs to be selected during design.

issue_context.summary: Mouse Without Borders loses both manually entered connection values immediately after Connect, even when the request does not connect or show an error.
known_information: PowerToys version 0.101.2362 from WinGet is affected.
The affected module is Mouse Without Borders.
The reporter entered a security key and device name, clicked Connect, and saw both fields wiped with no connection.
Test-NetConnection to the target on TCP port 15101 succeeded.
The live issue has one automated triage comment and no linked fix.
inferences: The field wipe is likely caused by unconditional UI cleanup after the async request rather than by the network failure itself.
The existing async request contract may need a success result or explicit error state before the UI can decide when to clear input.
issue_context.analysis: The current source confirms the core data-loss path, so a full design is more useful than requesting another generic log bundle. The remaining implementation choice is to use the existing request success/error contract without exposing or duplicating the security key.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the full issue body and the automated triage comment through 2026-09-24T18:44:07Z.
Confirmed the XAML names ConnectSecurityKeyTextBox and ConnectPCNameTextBox and the code-behind clears both after SubmitConnectionRequestAsync.

actions.label: Design preserve-on-failure fix
actions.note: Approve a focused fork-side design investigation; this action does not write upstream.

reproduce.title: Verify Mouse Without Borders preserves failed connection input
prerequisites: A second device name and security key that produce a failed or rejected connection attempt
Mouse Without Borders Settings open to the encryption-key connection fields
steps: Enter the security key and device name manually.
Click Connect and wait for the request to finish or report failure.
Observe whether either field is cleared and whether an error is shown.
Repeat with a known successful connection if available.
reproduce.expected_result: Failed attempts preserve both manually entered values for correction/retry; successful connection clears them only after success.

design.root_cause: MouseWithoutBordersPage.Connect performs unconditional post-request cleanup instead of tying cleanup to a successful connection result.
evidence: MouseWithoutBordersPage.xaml.cs reads both fields, awaits SubmitConnectionRequestAsync, then clears both TextBox values.
The issue reproduces the same sequence with no connection and no visible error.

affected_files.purpose: Owns the Connect command and currently clears the user inputs unconditionally.
Defines the async connection request result/error behavior consumed by the page.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The page cannot distinguish successful completion from a failed or rejected request when deciding whether to clear inputs.
implementation_steps.change: Expose or preserve an explicit success/error outcome using the existing MVVM notification pattern without returning the security key.
edge_cases: Do not log or persist the raw security key.
Preserve values on exceptions and rejected connections.
Keep existing error notification behavior visible to the user.
tests: Unit-test success, rejected connection, and exception outcomes.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Both TextBox values are set to String.Empty after every awaited request.
implementation_steps.change: Clear the fields only when the request outcome indicates a confirmed successful connection; otherwise leave the current user input intact.
edge_cases: Do not clear either field if only one value is invalid.
Keep retry behavior available after a timeout or unreachable target.
Avoid changing the existing reconnect command semantics.
tests: Add a focused page/view-model test proving values remain after failed submission and clear after success.

verify: Run the focused Mouse Without Borders Settings UI test project.
Manually reproduce a failed and successful connection attempt and inspect both fields.
risks: Changing the async result contract may affect other callers of SubmitConnectionRequestAsync.
A success signal must not expose the security key or alter existing connection persistence.
alternatives: A minimal try/catch around the existing call would preserve values on exceptions but would still risk clearing them on a rejected request; it is insufficient without an explicit success outcome.
